question: What are the trunks made of?
html:
Our trunks are made from recycled plastic bottles, about 11 per pair, and roughly 26M bottles had gone into our products through 2021 (Fair Harbor public filings). The exact fabric blend, lining material and trim components are not in the information we have, so we won't guess at them.

What we can confirm

  • Recycled plastic bottles. This is the material that defines the trunk. The figure of about 11 bottles per trunk comes from our public record (Fair Harbor public filings).
  • Cumulative bottles. About 26M bottles were used through 2021. The analysis uses this to cross-check est. cumulative sales of $60-80M through 2021, a low-confidence estimate (Fair Harbor public filings).
  • Sustainability is part of the brand. The growth plan describes Fair Harbor as a year-round sustainable lifestyle brand (Fair Harbor growth plan).

What is not covered here

QuestionStatusData that would answer it
Fabric blend (% recycled polyester, spandex)Not in contextProduct spec sheets, care labels
Liner material (e.g., mesh vs. compression)Not in contextProduct detail pages, supplier specs
Bottle count by style or sizeNot in contextSupplier material certificates
Bottles used since 2021Not in contextUpdated sourcing records

Beyond swim trunks

  • 64.0% of our 372 live products are non-swim (Fair Harbor growth plan).
  • Golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom launched in 2025-2026 (Fair Harbor growth plan).
  • The context does not say whether these newer lines use the same recycled-bottle fabric. Material composition by category would answer that.

How to check a product

  • Look at the fabric composition on the product page or the care label inside the garment.
  • For custom or team orders, ask for spec sheets before you order.

A clear, checkable materials story protects the full-price sell-through and wholesale buyer confidence the growth plan relies on. That matters because 38.5% of live variants are currently marked down, and the plan targets growth from ~250 to ~520 specialty doors (Fair Harbor growth plan).

Next actions

  1. Publish composition per product. Pull fabric blend, liner and trim specs from suppliers into one structured table for the website and the fit and CX agents.
  2. Refresh the bottle count. Update the cumulative recycled-bottle figure past 2021 using sourcing records, and confirm the ~11-per-trunk figure by style.
  3. Confirm non-swim materials. Document whether golf, kids and collegiate lines use recycled content, so wholesale reps can answer buyers consistently.
  4. Add claims to rep materials. Give the commissioned rep network verified material facts for golf pro shops, campus bookstores and coastal specialty doors.
